saints.name: St. Hyacinth
saints.title: Priest and Missionary
saints.shortBlurb: A Dominican friar called the Apostle of the North for his missions across Poland and the Slavic lands…
biography: Jacek Odrowąż was born about 1185 at Kamień in Silesia, of a noble family, and studied at Kraków, Prague, and Bologna before holding a canonry at Sandomierz. Travelling to Rome with his uncle Iwo, bishop of Kraków, he met Dominic de Guzmán there and in 1220 received the habit of the young Order of Preachers from Dominic's own hands.

Sent north to plant the order, he founded its first Polish houses, beginning with Kraków, and carried the Gospel as far as Kiev; later tradition stretches his journeys over Pomerania, Prussia, and the Scandinavian north, earning him the name Apostle of the North.

Legend cherishes him above all at the Mongol siege of Kiev in 1240, when he is said to have saved the ciborium and a stone statue of Our Lady, the burden his images still show him carrying. He died at Kraków on 15 August 1257 and was buried in its Dominican church; Clement VIII canonized him in 1594, and Poland and Lithuania keep him as patron.
saints.knownFor: Spreading the Dominican Order through the Slavic north.
